legend: This paraganglioma encircles the carotid bulb and partially surrounds the internal carotid artery.
This fibrotic SDHB-mutated paraganglioma encases the carotid artery and extends to the resection margins.
Areas with a nested Zellballen pattern are present focally at the periphery of the tumour, but the tumour mostly consists of small cells with solid and infiltrative growth.
S100 immunohistochemistry shows extremely rare sustentacular cells in these areas.

diagnosis: Local recurrence of a carotid body paraganglioma
legend: This neck mass was discovered on follow-up scanning in a patient with a germline SDHB mutation who had an ipsilateral sclerotic infiltrating paraganglioma resected 4 years earlier. The lesion was 4–8 mm in diameter and protruded from the lumen of a vein.

diagnosis: Local recurrence of a carotid body paraganglioma
legend: This neck mass was discovered on follow-up scanning in a patient with a germline SDHB mutation who had an ipsilateral sclerotic infiltrating paraganglioma resected 4 years earlier. In contrast to the initial tumour, which for the most part was highly cellular and consisted of small cells with infiltrative and solid growth patterns and extremely rare sustentacular cells, this tumour consists of larger cells with relatively well-formed nests and readily identified sustentacular cells (immunohistochemical stain for S100). The tumour was initially suspected of being a lymph node metastasis. Because no lymph node was present, it was considered to be a local recurrence, most likely from peripheral areas of the original neoplasm.

diagnosis: Local recurrence of a carotid body paraganglioma
legend: This neck mass was discovered on follow-up scanning in a patient with a germline SDHB mutation who had an ipsilateral sclerotic infiltrating paraganglioma resected 4 years earlier. The Ki-67 proliferation index was comparable with that in solid areas of the initial tumour.

This neck paraganglioma from an adolescent boy with an SDHB mutation and a history of gastrointestinal stromal tumour has prominent vacuoles and slightly eosinophilic cytoplasm, which is often seen in association with SDHB mutation. In this case there is abundant cytoplasm, but the Zellballen pattern is poorly formed.

legend: Classic anatomical and functional imaging characteristics in a patient imaged at 19 years of age. To assess potential surgical options, CT angiography was performed, further demarcating the lesion, which was deemed unresectable because of encasement of the internal and external carotid.

diagnosis: Structural and functional imaging studies in a carotid body paraganglioma
legend: Classic anatomical and functional imaging characteristics in a patient imaged at 19 years of age. To exclude metastases, 68Ga-DOTATOC PET-CT was performed, with bright labelling consistent with intense expression of SSTR. Genetic testing showed a germline SDHD mutation.

diagnosis: SSTR2A expression in a carotid body paraganglioma
legend: Diffuse strong expression of SSTR2A correlates with bright images in PET-CT using 68Ga-DOTATOC or other radiolabelled somatostatin analogues.

The spongy cut surface of this sporadic paraganglioma (shown here) corresponds histologically to cavernous blood vessels (see Fig. <<27036>>) that communicate with vessels in the tumour capsule. Prominent, well-formed nests of clear tumour cells are highlighted by immunohistochemical stains for S100 (see Fig. <<27037>>; nuclear and cytoplasmic) and SOX10 (not shown; nuclear). Note the intratumoural variation in density of sustentacular cells, with a gradient in this case from the periphery to the centre. A small nerve outside the tumour is present at the lower right.

The relative levels of expression of neuroendocrine markers in this apparently sporadic carotid body paraganglioma are those generally seen in other head and neck parasympathetic paragangliomas, including chromogranin A (shown here) and tyrosine hydroxylase (see Fig. <<27041>>). Chromogranin A can be expressed in a patchy pattern, and often in only a dot-like cytoplasmic distribution. Tyrosine hydroxylase is often absent or focal.

This tumour was removed in an en bloc resection followed by a synthetic carotid artery graft. The patient, who was 22 years old when the tumour was discovered, was found to have a germline SDHB mutation.

This paraganglioma involved the middle ear, where bone remodeling and involvement is a relatively common occurrence, and does not affect prognosis. There is a zellballen architecture with cells that show focal nuclear pleomorphism.
